THE ASSERTION UNDER TEST. The read-only for-loop tool call is gated even though it only reads (ls) -- live-confirmed the classifier escalates on shell control-flow syntax, not on read/write status. kind:"approval" "requested" opens with presentation_phase:human_pending under --approval-judge off; TranscriptPermissionPending -> waiting via state_classifier.go's transcript_permission_prompt rule.

The driver's raw keypress ("1" = Yes, proceed, no trailing Enter) answers the prompt; kind:"approval" "decision_applied" (decision_source.kind expected human_approval) closes it, the ls executes, and the session returns to working while the model reads the tool result and proposes the second tool call

The touch&&rm&&echo call's rm stage is gated (per-stage evaluation: touch is skipped as safe, rm needs approval) -- the SAME mutating-gate mechanism 2-19 already exercises, reused here to give the read-only episode a mutating sibling in one recording. This is the half the scenario's acceptance criteria already expect any permission-gating agent to cover.

The driver's second raw keypress ("1" = Allow this stage once) answers the prompt; kind:"approval" "decision_applied" closes it and the session returns to working while the approved command runs and the agent continues toward its final reply
Turn completes back to ready on the same session once the final reply (PERMISSION_GATE_NONMUTATING_OK) lands; state must not bounce back to waiting afterward
Trailing idle: the session stays ready for >=10s after the last dialog closes, catching a session left pinned at, or falling back to, waiting
